findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:396-416 — MEDIUM: validatePromptEnvelope treats every optional field as merely nonblank, so digest-bearing fields such as toolPolicyDigest and systemInstructionDigest accept arbitrary strings. Runtime reproduction with toolPolicyDigest="not-a-digest" prints MALFORMED_OPTIONAL_DIGEST_ACCEPTED. This contradicts CHK-001 adversarial schema intent requiring malformed digest values to fail closed and leaves the foundational Story-2 envelope schema permissive before it becomes gate-bound. Split optional digest fields from optional text/reference fields and validate each digest with requireDigest; add mutation probes for all optional digest-bearing fields.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 973f9ce95a: PromptEnvelope optional material/storyFiles/policy/tool/system digest fields now use requireDigest; focused smoke mutates every optional digest and requires explicit rejection.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:161-198 — MEDIUM: canonicalJsonStringify enumerates only Object.keys and therefore silently drops symbol-keyed own properties instead of rejecting non-CanonicalJson input. Runtime reproduction canonicalJsonStringify({a:1,[Symbol("hidden")]:2}) returns {"a":1}, allowing two structurally different inputs to collapse to the same canonical bytes/digest. This directly violates CHK-001 canonical-fail-closed intent that unsupported values must not disappear or produce an admissible digest. Reject own symbol keys (and cover the mutation in the focused smoke) before canonicalizing object entries.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 973f9ce95a: canonical serializer rejects own symbol keys before enumeration; focused smoke proves symbol-keyed input cannot collapse to canonical bytes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:249 The supposedly frozen lifecycle registry does not fail closed on replacement drift. validatePromptRoleContracts checks membership, the 12/3/1 partition, retired-channel/default status, and compatibility status, but never verifies the accepted exact mappings (test-intent/test-case-reviewer -> verification-intent and implementation-reviewer -> quality+behavior guidance). Reproducer against the built module: clone PROMPT_ROLE_CONTRACTS, change test-intent.replacementAgentType to lattice-review-quality, then call validatePromptRoleContracts(...); it returns successfully (ACCEPTED_INVALID_REPLACEMENT). This directly violates CHK-004's requirement that replacement metadata violating frozen policy be rejected and would let a semantically different compatibility migration target retain an admissible registry shape.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 973f9ce95a: RoleContract validation compares exact replacementAgentType and migrationHint against frozen policies; replacement and guidance mutations now reject.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:127 canonicalJsonStringify enumerates objects with Object.keys(), so unsupported own symbol keys and non-enumerable own fields silently disappear instead of failing closed. A plain object with a=1, one with an own Symbol key whose value is undefined, and one with a non-enumerable own hidden=undefined all serialize to the same {a:1} canonical JSON and produce the same domain-separated digest. That contradicts CHK-001's explicit invariant that unsupported/undefined values cannot disappear or collapse to an admissible digest, and it creates a content-address collision class before PromptEnvelope uses this primitive. Reject non-string/non-enumerable own keys (or otherwise mechanically constrain the accepted object domain) and add mutation probes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 973f9ce95a: canonical serializer rejects symbol-keyed, non-enumerable, and accessor own fields; focused probes cover all three disappearance classes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-contract-measurement-smoke.ts:100-205 and 327-335 — HIGH: the focused smoke never deletes a required field from RuntimeContract, RoleContract, PromptMeasurementRecord, or PromptEnvelope. It tests unknown/invalid values, but the must adversarial intent and recorded evidence explicitly claim missing required fields fail closed. A regression that stops requiring one field could therefore pass this suite. Add representative required-key deletion probes for all four schemas (ideally table-driven) and rerun the bound evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 973f9ce95a: table-driven deletion probes remove every required key from RuntimeContract, RoleContract, PromptMeasurementRecord, and PromptEnvelope and require fail-closed rejection.

findings.desc: scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.mjs:2291-2409 — MEDIUM: --probe-baseline-drift mutates structuredClone(current) and compares two in-memory snapshots; it never changes one actual assembled Prompt/template, observes the normal verifier fail on bytes/hash, restores the source, and observes PASS. CHK-004 adversarial:2 requires that exact integration/restore path, while its evidence note accurately says only synthetic mutations. Add a non-destructive temp-worktree or injectable collector integration probe that exercises the real collection boundary and proves repository restoration.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 973f9ce95a: verifier copies the real registry to an OS temp directory, collects pristine source/assembled output, mutates a copied prompt, proves normal registry/output bytes-hash comparisons fail, restores in finally, proves pass, and removes temp state; protected repository paths remain unchanged.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:178-185 — HIGH: the round-2 canonicalization fix validates hidden/accessor/symbol own fields only for plain objects; arrays return before that validation and still silently discard extra own state. Runtime repros show an array [1] with Symbol("hidden")=2, hidden=2, or an enumerable accessor derived all serialize as [1] (ACCEPTED), so distinct unsupported inputs still collapse to identical canonical bytes/digests. This is the same fail-closed root class as resolved F-002/F-004 and still violates CHK-001 canonical-fail-closed. Validate array own keys/descriptors too, allowing only dense numeric indices plus the intrinsic length data property, and add symbol/string/accessor array probes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29789e7eeb: arrays accept only intrinsic length and exact dense enumerable data indices; symbol, extra string, non-enumerable and accessor own state rejects with focused probes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:178 F-004 is only partially fixed: the new Reflect.ownKeys fail-closed checks run only in the plain-object branch, while arrays return at line 184 after validating numeric indices only. Arrays carrying an own Symbol key, an extra enumerable string field, or a non-enumerable/accessor field still serialize and hash byte-identically to the plain array, so unsupported values continue to disappear. Reproducer: compare canonicalJsonStringify([1]) with arrays mutated by arr[Symbol(...)]=undefined, arr.hidden=undefined, or defineProperty(arr,'hidden',{value:undefined,enumerable:false}); all return [1] with the same digest. The CHK-001 invariant covers nested object/array values and requires all otherwise non-canonical input to fail closed; validate array own keys/descriptors as well and add corresponding probes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29789e7eeb by the same complete array own-key/descriptor validation; extra enumerable/non-enumerable/malformed keys and symbol keys cannot disappear into an admissible digest.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:272 The F-003 repair freezes only replacementAgentType and migrationHint, not the documented lifecycle/default policy. validatePromptRoleContracts still accepts an active canonical role such as lattice-evaluator with defaultDispatch changed from true to false; it also accepts a responsibility mutation while retaining the old semanticDigest. The first case directly violates CHK-004's requirement that defaultDispatch drift from the frozen role policy fail closed and the plan rule that active role/default dispatch remain aligned. Reproducer against the rebuilt module maps lattice-evaluator to {...contract,defaultDispatch:false}; validatePromptRoleContracts returns successfully (active-default-false ACCEPTED). Compare each row's status/defaultDispatch and semantic policy fields or recompute/verify the semantic digest, and add an active-default mutation probe.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29789e7eeb: validator compares every policy-derived RoleContract field against exact ROLE_POLICIES and recomputes semanticDigest; defaultDispatch, responsibility, policy arrays and digest mutation probes reject.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-contract-measurement-smoke.ts:75-88 — HIGH: canonical fail-closed coverage only probes symbol/non-enumerable/accessor fields on plain objects, not arrays. Independent runtime repro confirms arrays carrying each of those own-state forms are still ACCEPTED as [1] because packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:178-185 returns before own-key/descriptor validation. This leaves CHK-001 prompt-contract-canonical-fail-closed uncovered and permits distinct inputs to collapse to one digest. Add array variants for symbol-keyed, extra string-keyed (enumerable and non-enumerable), and accessor fields, then bind refreshed evidence after fixing the array validator.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29789e7eeb: adversarial smoke covers array symbol keys, extra enumerable/non-enumerable strings, accessor extra/index fields, non-enumerable indices, malformed indices and sparse arrays.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:178 F-008 still does not close the full array runtime domain: Array.isArray accepts array subclasses and arrays with custom prototypes, but the implementation does not require the ordinary Array prototype and invokes candidate.map through the untrusted prototype. A subclass can override map() so canonicalJsonStringify of a one-element array returns the invalid/non-canonical string [MALICIOUS]; a custom prototype preserving Array.prototype.map plus hidden inherited state serializes and hashes identically to [1]. This breaks determinism/fail-closed canonicalization even though own-key probes now pass. Require the supported array prototype/domain and invoke the intrinsic Array.prototype.map (or iterate indices without prototype dispatch), with subclass/custom-prototype mutation probes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 181771de4b: canonical arrays require Object.getPrototypeOf(candidate)===Array.prototype and serialize by explicit index loop over validated own data descriptors; subclass/custom prototypes reject before any candidate method invocation.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-contract-measurement-smoke.ts:89-109 — HIGH: the expanded array mutation matrix still omits Array subclasses/custom prototypes and prototype-dispatched map behavior. Independent repro against current dist shows an Array subclass overriding map serializes as invalid [MALICIOUS], while an Array with a custom prototype carrying hidden inherited state serializes as [1]. Because packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts invokes candidate.map and does not restrict the array prototype, CHK-001 canonical-fail-closed remains uncovered. Add subclass, overridden-map, and custom-prototype probes and require ordinary Array.prototype (or intrinsic index iteration) before refreshing evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 181771de4b: smoke proves malicious subclass map and candidate-owned map are never invoked, custom inherited state rejects, and ordinary dense arrays serialize deterministically.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:165-211 — HIGH: canonicalJsonStringify still accepts Proxy-wrapped arrays. Array.isArray(proxy) is true and the proxy can report Array.prototype, while hasOwnProperty/Reflect.ownKeys/Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor invoke attacker-controlled traps. A minimal proxy whose getOwnPropertyDescriptor returns an incrementing value for index 0 serializes the unchanged same proxy as [3] on the first call and [6] on the second. Thus the canonical/digest entry point is neither deterministic nor side-effect-free for an unsupported runtime structure, violating CHK-001 deterministic and canonical-fail-closed intents. Reject Proxy inputs before array/object traversal (for example Node util.types.isProxy) and add array plus plain-object proxy probes proving no traps are consumed into admissible bytes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 04e9e4385d: util.types.isProxy rejects every Proxy before Array.isArray, prototype, ownKeys or descriptor traversal; stateful array Proxy cannot produce bytes or trigger traps.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-contract-measurement-smoke.ts:61-134 — HIGH: canonical fail-closed/determinism coverage omits Proxy-wrapped arrays and objects. Independent repro against current dist uses an array Proxy with a stateful getOwnPropertyDescriptor trap; canonicalJsonStringify of the unchanged proxy returns [3] then [6]. The candidate traversal consumes proxy traps into admissible canonical bytes, so CHK-001 deterministic-algorithm and canonical-fail-closed intents remain uncovered. Reject Proxy inputs before traversal and add array/object Proxy probes, including stateful descriptor/ownKeys traps, proving no proxy yields an admissible digest.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 04e9e4385d: smoke covers instrumented plain-object and stateful array Proxies with zero traps invoked, revoked Proxy rejection, and unchanged normal plain inputs.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:322 and packages/main/src/core/prompt-measurement.ts:87-154,175-183 — HIGH: PROMPT_ROLE_CONTRACTS freezes only the outer array; every exported RoleContract row and nested policy array remains mutable, and report generation never re-runs validatePromptRoleContracts. Runtime repro: Object.isFrozen(PROMPT_ROLE_CONTRACTS[0]) is false; changing the first compatibility row status to retired makes generatePromptMeasurementReport emit partition 12/2/2, and verifyPromptMeasurementReport accepts it because recomputation consumes the same corrupted singleton. This violates CHK-002 exact frozen 12/3/1 lifecycle registry and CHK-003 fail-closed reporting. Deep-freeze each contract and nested array before export and/or validate the registry at report consumption; add direct mutation probes showing writes throw/fail and a corrupted supplied registry cannot yield an accepted report.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 0913871be0: PROMPT_ROLE_CONTRACTS now deeply freezes every row and all nested array structures. The smoke test uses a strict child process to attempt row-status and nested-array mutations and requires either a throw or unchanged state; report aggregation remains 12/3/1.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-contract-measurement-smoke.ts:335-456 — HIGH: coverage proves construction-time role-policy mutations reject, but never tests post-export mutation of PROMPT_ROLE_CONTRACTS or report-time revalidation. Independent child-process repro shows the outer registry is frozen while rows/nested arrays are mutable; changing one compatibility row to retired yields a 12/2/2 report that verifyPromptMeasurementReport accepts. This leaves CHK-002 exact frozen partition and CHK-003 role-set fail-closed intents uncovered. Add strict-mode mutation probes for rows and nested arrays plus a corrupted-registry/report-consumer probe that must reject, backed by deep freeze and/or consumption-time validation.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 0913871be0: generatePromptMeasurementReport validates the exported singleton against current expected role IDs before any consumption. Child probes show semantic digest mutation cannot corrupt the frozen singleton, a corrupted foreign clone is rejected fail-closed, and the generated report remains 12/3/1.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/validate-concept.ts:125 and :372 Extension filtering uses only the diff header's b/new path (DiffFileSources.file = header[2]), so renaming a supported source file to an unsupported extension hides a real deletion. Reproducer: a diff from a/src/removed.ts to b/docs/removed.md deleting `export function realDeletion()` and adding Markdown prose yields analyzeDeletedSymbols(...) = {symbols:[], diagnostics:[]}. The same bypass applies to JS/Python renamed to JSON/Markdown/text. This violates the round-8 requirement that bounded filtering not hide real TS/JS/Python deletions. Track oldPath and newPath separately, parse each side according to its own supported extension/script kind, and add supported-to-unsupported rename probes; malformed supported old/new sides must remain fail closed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 3fd29d4993: diff reconstruction now retains independent oldPath/newPath including /dev/null and parses each side only according to its own supported language family. Supported-to-unsupported renames remain deletions, additions do not fabricate deletions, path-bound supported renames preserve explicit identity, and malformed supported sides still fail closed.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/concept-gate-scope-smoke.ts:122-141 — HIGH: mixed-artifact coverage omits supported-source to unsupported-artifact renames. Independent repro renaming src/removed.ts to docs/removed.md while deleting export function realDeletion returns symbols=[] and diagnostics=[] because analyzeDeletedSymbols classifies both sides by the new path. This leaves the round-8 real TS/JS/Python deletion guarantee bypassable. Add TS/JS/Python supported→unsupported and unsupported→supported rename probes, plus malformed supported old/new side cases; bind each side to its own path/parser so real deletions remain visible and malformed source remains fail closed.
